ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Martin Luther

code.originalText: Thirteen-week review: attacks, repeat audiogram, mood, and the 24-hour urine for stone prevention

text.paragraph: Thirteen-week review: attacks, hearing, mood and stone prevention. [S]

Professor Luther returns five weeks after his six-week review. He has had no vertigo attack for eight weeks and has preached and lectured without one. The tinnitus is still there but quieter. He has done the printed balance exercises daily; the first appointment with the vestibular physical therapist is next week, because of a waiting list. He collected the 24-hour urine on an ordinary working day. He keeps the salt limit at home but not at dinners with guests, and he admits he drinks little water. His mood is clearly better: he sleeps seven hours, enjoys his work and his household again, and has had eight therapy sessions. He has no thoughts of harming himself. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Blood pressure 120/78, pulse 70; weight 84.4 kg, BMI 27.6
No nystagmus; tandem gait steady; Romberg steady on foam with eyes closed
Euthymic, reactive affect; no suicidal ideation

Recurrent attacks of spinning vertigo for about three months, the worst twelve days ago, lasting hours, with roaring tinnitus, fullness and muffled hearing in the left ear and nausea, the tinnitus persisting between attacks; with low mood, poor sleep and loss of interest; cause not established at intake: an inner-ear disorder suspected, with vestibular migraine, vestibular schwannoma and posterior circulation stroke to be excluded and depression to be assessed; otology consultation requested
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to his documented attacks of April and July 1527; superseded by the diagnoses at the second visit.

Ménière disease of the left ear, definite (AAO-HNS 2020 and Bárány Society criteria), with low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and persistent tinnitus in the left ear; vestibular migraine considered and judged unlikely as the main cause; vestibular schwannoma excluded by MRI
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the otology consultation, linked to his documented attacks and to the retrospective diagnosis of Ménière disease (R).

Major depressive disorder, recurrent, moderate (DSM-5-TR), with low mood, poor sleep, loss of interest, guilt and fatigue for about two months, after earlier periods of spiritual crisis and low mood; no suicidal ideation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis linked to his documented Anfechtungen and low periods; not a claim that he was so diagnosed; the retrospective psychiatric readings are disputed (R).
Urinary stone disease: one stone passed spontaneously last year after severe pain; stone type and metabolic risk not yet known at intake
S — Synthetic modern problem anchored to his documented first stone in 1526.

Right distal ureteral stone, 5 mm, at the ureterovesical junction, with mild right hydronephrosis and renal colic; no infection; kidney function normal; managed with naproxen and tamsulosin; passed nine days later; resolved
S — Synthetic acute problem anchored to his documented recurrent stones; this episode is not a historical claim.

list.item:
Ménière disease of the left ear, controlled (H81.02). No attacks for eight weeks. Repeat audiogram: the left low-frequency loss has improved to 30 to 35 dB, with word recognition 92 percent. Sodium 137 and potassium 3.8 mmol/L on the thiazide. Intratympanic steroid is not needed. [S]
Continue hydrochlorothiazide and the salt limit.
Vestibular therapy as booked.
Audiogram with any change in hearing, and yearly.
Tinnitus counseling offered; hearing aid not needed now.

Recurrent calcium oxalate stones (Z87.442). 24-hour urine: volume 1.6 liters (low), sodium 140 mmol (high, about 3,200 mg of sodium), citrate 410 mg (low), calcium 190 mg, oxalate 38 mg and uric acid 680 mg (normal); creatinine 1,750 mg shows a complete collection. The calcium is normal on the thiazide. Low volume, high sodium and low citrate are the targets. [S]
Drink enough to pass at least 2.5 liters of urine a day: a full glass with each meal and at each lecture break.
Dietitian referral for sodium below 2,300 mg a day, which also helps the Ménière disease.
Normal dietary calcium; lemon or orange in water for citrate; potassium citrate if citrate stays low.
Continue hydrochlorothiazide.
Repeat 24-hour urine in about six months.

Recurrent depression, responding (F33.1). PHQ-9 6, a 60 percent fall from 15: response, not yet remission. [S]
Continue sertraline 50 mg for at least six to twelve months after remission, given a recurrent course.
Continue therapy every two weeks.
Safety plan reviewed and unchanged; 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and the clinic number confirmed.
